prs.title: feat: Ads-Client Provides fix for images_or_spocs ordering issue
prs.bug: A #[serde(untagged)] enum listed Image before Spoc, and since an Image's fields are a subset of a Spoc's, every spoc deserialized as an image.
prs.rule: Flag #[serde(untagged)] enums where an earlier variant's required fields are a subset of a later variant's (earlier variant shadows later) unless it uses deny_unknown_fields or carries an explicit discriminator.
prs.detect: syn-based custom lint/CI script: for each enum with #[serde(untagged)], resolve struct-typed variants in the crate, compute required (non-Option, non-#[serde(default)]) field sets, report i<j where fields(i) ⊆ fields(j) and variant i lacks #[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]; lower-noise variant: require every untagged enum to have a round-trip test per variant.

prs.title: Fix breadcrumbs field in error support
prs.bug: A rename made the tracing macro emit `breadcrumb_string` instead of `breadcrumbs` (field name comes from the variable name), crashing the Android error reporter that expected `breadcrumbs`.
prs.rule: Events sent to the `app-services-error-reporter::*` targets must use explicitly named fields from a fixed schema (error: message, type_name, breadcrumbs; breadcrumb: message, module, line, column).
prs.detect: CI regex/ast-grep over `tracing_support::(error|info)!(target: "app-services-error-reporter::...", ...)` extracting field identifiers (shorthand `x` counts as field `x`), compared to the schema; plus a unit test that captures the event with an EventSink and asserts field names (the test 7658 added).

prs.title: fix(ads-client): panic on a malformed OHTTP preflight response
prs.bug: `From<PreflightResponse> for Headers` called .expect() on header inserts using server-echoed geo/UA values, so non-ASCII or CRLF values panicked the host process.
prs.rule: Deny clippy::unwrap_used / expect_used / panic_in_result_fn in non-test component code; require #[expect(..., reason = "...")] for proven invariants (ratchet with a baseline). Conversions from server data must be TryFrom.
prs.detect: [workspace.lints.clippy] unwrap_used = "warn", expect_used = "warn", panic_in_result_fn = "warn" (+ allow_attributes_without_reason) applied to components/*/src with tests exempted (allow-unwrap-in-tests / allow-expect-in-tests in clippy.toml); fail CI on new hits vs a stored baseline. clippy::expect_used flags the two `.expect("valid header")` calls directly.

prs.title: tabs: don't log the entire tabs payload at trace level.
prs.bug: The tabs sync engine logged the full outgoing TabsRecord with {:?} at trace level, leaking tab URLs/titles (PII) and flooding desktop logs.
prs.rule: Never Debug-format sync records/payloads or other user-data types in log macros; such types get a redacting Display/Debug.
prs.detect: Custom lint (dylint) or ast-grep: in trace!/debug!/info!/warn!/error! args, flag `{:?}`/`{x:?}` applied to values whose type is in a 'sensitive types' list (types in */sync/record.rs, *Record, *Payload, Login*, Tabs*) or derives Serialize+Debug in sync modules.

prs.title: Bug 2062772 - Fixes issues with updating the remote settings client dumps
prs.bug: viaduct-hyper parsed a relative Location header with Url::parse instead of joining it to the request URL, and the dump CLI built a bundle URL with format!("{}/...") producing a double slash (404).
prs.rule: Build and resolve URLs with url::Url APIs (join / path_segments_mut), not format!/string concatenation; resolve Location headers against the request URL.
prs.detect: ast-grep: `format!("{}/$$$", $U, $$$)` / `format!("{$U}/...")` where $U's identifier matches /url|base/i; and `Url::parse($X)` where $X derives from a header named location.

prs.title: Bug 2045937 - Fix no return in unenrollFromAllFirefoxLabs

The Kotlin compiler then reports 'A return expression required in a function with a block body'.

prs.title: Fix disconnecting an account after starting to reauth it.

prs.title: Fix PKCS#11 struct packing on Windows to match NSS 1-byte alignment
prs.bug: On Windows, NSS PKCS#11 structs use 1-byte packing, but the Rust bindings declared them as plain #[repr(C)], giving a layout mismatch.
prs.rule: Hand-written FFI structs must have per-target layout assertions generated from the C headers.
prs.detect: Generate size/align/offset assertions with bindgen against pkcs11t.h for each target (including x86_64-pc-windows-msvc with #pragma pack(1)) and compile them in CI (`cargo check --target x86_64-pc-windows-msvc -p nss_sys`); flag #[repr(C)] structs in nss_sys/src/bindings with no matching layout test.

rules.title: Never panic in UniFFI lifts or conversions of foreign/server data
rules.problem: unwrap()/expect() inside uniffi::custom_type! try_lift (and in From impls over server responses) turns bad input from Kotlin/Swift/JS or the server into a hard crash of the host app.
rules.rule: No panicking constructs (unwrap/expect/panic!/unreachable!/assert!) inside uniffi::custom_type! try_lift closures or conversions of foreign/server data; return Err instead.
rules.detect: ast-grep rule matching `uniffi::custom_type!($T, $F, { $$$ try_lift: $BODY $$$ })` where $BODY contains `.unwrap()`, `.expect(`, `panic!`, `unreachable!`; same check for `impl From<$X> for $Y` whose source type is a deserialized server response (suggest TryFrom). Today it would also flag places/src/lib.rs VisitTransitionSet try_lift `.expect(...)`.
rules.false_positive_risk: low - try_lift already returns Result, so any panic there is almost certainly wrong.

rules.title: Deny unwrap/expect/assert in non-test component code
rules.problem: Panics in FFI-reachable Rust (unwrap on Option, expect on fallible header inserts, assert! in serializers) crash Firefox processes instead of returning errors.
rules.rule: Deny clippy::unwrap_used / expect_used / panic_in_result_fn in non-test component code; require #[expect(..., reason = "...")] for proven invariants (ratchet with a baseline).
rules.detect: [workspace.lints.clippy] unwrap_used = "warn", expect_used = "warn", panic_in_result_fn = "warn" (+ allow_attributes_without_reason) applied to components/*/src with tests exempted (allow-unwrap-in-tests / allow-expect-in-tests in clippy.toml); fail CI on new hits vs a stored baseline.
rules.false_positive_risk: medium - many existing invariant unwraps; needs a baseline/ratchet and #[expect(clippy::expect_used, reason=...)] for proven invariants.

rules.title: Log only through tracing-support macros
rules.problem: Calls to log::*! or raw tracing::event! bypass the tracing_support event sink, so logs and error reports silently disappear.
rules.rule: Components must log only through tracing-support / error-support macros, never `log::*!` or raw `tracing::event!`/`tracing::*!`.
rules.detect: clippy.toml `disallowed-macros = ["log::trace","log::debug","log::info","log::warn","log::error","tracing::event","tracing::trace","tracing::debug","tracing::info","tracing::warn","tracing::error"]` with #[allow] only inside components/support/tracing; plus a cargo-metadata check that no component/example crate depends on `log` directly. Would flag current uses in components/relay/src/{rs,lib}.rs and components/crashtest.
rules.false_positive_risk: low - one allowlisted crate (components/support/tracing); examples can opt out explicitly.

rules.title: Validate error-reporter tracing event fields against a schema
rules.problem: tracing takes field names from variable names, so renaming a local silently changes the cross-language contract with the Android/iOS error reporters (lost details, crashes).
rules.rule: Events sent to the `app-services-error-reporter::*` targets must use explicitly named fields from a fixed schema (error: message, type_name, breadcrumbs; breadcrumb: message, module, line, column).
rules.detect: CI regex/ast-grep over `tracing_support::(error|info)!(target: "app-services-error-reporter::...", ...)` extracting field identifiers (shorthand `x` counts as field `x`), compared to the schema; plus a unit test that captures the event with an EventSink and asserts field names (the test 7658 added).
rules.false_positive_risk: low - only a handful of call sites target app-services-error-reporter.

rules.title: Prefix report_error labels with the owning component
rules.problem: Copy-pasted report_error labels attribute errors to the wrong component in dashboards.
rules.rule: report_error!/ErrorHandling::report_error labels must start with a prefix registered for the crate they are in.
rules.detect: Grep `report_error!("X` and `.report_error("X` per crate directory, compare against a per-crate prefix allowlist (remote_settings: remote-settings-; fxa-client: fxa-client-, fxaclient-, fxa-state-machine-; sync15: incoming-, invalid-incoming-, ...).
rules.false_positive_risk: medium - existing labels use inconsistent prefixes (fxaclient- vs fxa-client-, incoming-), so an allowlist is needed.

rules.title: Assert every mockito mock in tests
rules.problem: mockito 0.31 does not enforce .expect(N) unless .assert() is called; `let _m = mock(...)` tests pass while the code under test does the wrong thing.
rules.rule: Bind each mock to a non-underscore name and call .assert() before the test ends (or wrap mocks in a helper that asserts on Drop).
rules.detect: ast-grep in #[test] fns: `let _$M = $$$mock($$$)$$$.create()` or a `let $M = mock(...)` with no subsequent `$M.assert()`.
rules.false_positive_risk: low - deliberate 'any number of calls' mocks can use `.expect_at_least(0)` plus assert or an allow comment.

rules.title: Exclude android/ and ios/ from published crates
rules.problem: Crates without `exclude = ["/android", "/ios"]` vendor Kotlin/Swift sources into mozilla-firefox third_party/rust.
rules.rule: Every workspace crate with android/ or ios/ subdirectories must exclude them in [package].
rules.detect: cargo metadata + filesystem check: package dir has android/ or ios/ => package.exclude contains "/android"/"/ios" or package.include is set. Currently flags components/fxcontainers and components/support/db-crypto.
rules.false_positive_risk: low - purely structural check.

rules.title: Forbid component dependencies on examples/ crates
rules.problem: A support tool depending on examples/cli-support pulled NSS linking and heavy deps into the wrong place.
rules.rule: Crates under components/ may not have normal/build dependencies on crates under examples/ (dev-dependencies allowed).
rules.detect: Script over `cargo metadata --format-version 1`: map package ids to manifest paths; fail if a components/** package depends (kind != dev) on an examples/** package.
rules.false_positive_risk: low - structural.

rules.title: Run mozilla-central's whitespace, license and XDG linters in a-s CI
rules.problem: Violations are only found when a-s is imported into mozilla-central (trailing whitespace/CRLF/EOF newline, missing MPL headers, hard-coded ~/.mozilla paths), costing follow-up PRs.
rules.rule: a-s CI runs equivalents of m-c's file-whitespace, license and dot-mozilla-reference linters on changed files.
rules.detect: editorconfig-checker or `git diff --check` style script (no trailing whitespace, LF only, single final newline); MPL header check on *.rs/*.kt/*.swift/*.py/*.sh; grep for '\.mozilla' outside an allowlist of XDG-aware files.
rules.false_positive_risk: low - same rules m-c already enforces; fixtures/binary files need excludes.

rules.title: Shellcheck and portability-check build scripts
rules.problem: Build/import scripts break on the other platform's shell or sed (BSD `sed -i ''`, bash-5 'bad substitution', bash-3.2 empty arrays under set -u).
rules.rule: Run shellcheck on all scripts, ban `sed -i` in cross-platform scripts and `${#arr[@]:-...}`, and smoke-run argument parsing under bash 3.2 and bash 5.
rules.detect: shellcheck -x on **/*.sh; regexes `sed\s+-i` (outside annotated macOS-only scripts like libs/build-nss-ios.sh) and `\$\{#\w+\[@\]:-`; bash -n plus a no-arg dry run. megazords/ios-rust/build-xcframework.sh:183 still contains `${#GENERATE_ARGS[@]:-0}` (bad substitution in bash 5.2).
rules.false_positive_risk: low - few scripts; macOS-only scripts get an explicit annotation.

rules.title: Build Kotlin/Swift automatically when platform code changes
rules.problem: Normal PR CI skips module-build and swift tasks unless the title contains [ci full], so Kotlin compile errors and iOS script breakage land on main.
rules.rule: If a PR touches components/**/android/**, *.kt, *.swift, megazords/ios-rust/** or build-xcframework.sh, the corresponding platform build/test tasks run automatically.
rules.detect: In taskcluster/app_services_taskgraph (get_decision_parameters/target_tasks), compute changed files and include run-on-pr-type=full-ci tasks for the matching platform.
rules.false_positive_risk: low - costs CI time only, no false alarms.

rules.title: Use C ABI type aliases and check nss_sys for Windows
rules.problem: Hand-written NSS/PKCS#11 bindings used fixed-width u64 for CK_ULONG constants and #[repr(C)] where Windows needs 1-byte packing, breaking the Windows build/ABI.
rules.rule: Constants and struct fields mirroring C `unsigned long` use CK_ULONG/c_ulong; every #[repr(C)] binding struct has per-target layout assertions; nss_sys is type-checked for a Windows target in CI.
rules.detect: Regex `pub const CK[A-Z]*_\w+\s*:\s*u64` in nss_sys/src/bindings; `cargo check --target x86_64-pc-windows-msvc -p nss_sys -p nss`; bindgen-generated layout tests (size/align/offset) per target compared with the hand-written structs.
rules.false_positive_risk: low - narrow scope (nss_sys bindings).

rules.title: Wrap raw NSS allocations in RAII and run LeakSanitizer
rules.problem: Manual SECITEM_AllocItem/SECITEM_FreeItem pairs leak on early returns; leaks were only caught by mozilla-central's LSan.
rules.rule: Raw NSS alloc/free functions are only callable from RAII wrapper types; rc_crypto/nss tests run under LeakSanitizer in a-s CI.
rules.detect: clippy.toml disallowed-methods for nss_sys::SECITEM_AllocItem, SECITEM_FreeItem, PORT_Alloc*, PK11_Free* etc. with #[allow] only in nss/src/util.rs wrappers; CI job `RUSTFLAGS=-Zsanitizer=leak cargo +nightly test -p nss -p rc_crypto`.
rules.false_positive_risk: low - wrappers get an explicit allow.

rules.title: Flag shadowing variants in #[serde(untagged)] enums
rules.problem: With untagged enums serde picks the first variant that deserializes; a variant whose fields are a subset of a later one swallows the later variant's data.
rules.rule: For untagged enums, no earlier variant may have a required-field set that is a subset of a later variant's unless it uses deny_unknown_fields; otherwise use an explicit tag/discriminator.
rules.detect: syn-based script: parse enums with #[serde(untagged)], resolve variant struct types in the crate, compute required field sets (skip Option/#[serde(default)]), report i<j with fields(i) ⊆ fields(j).
rules.false_positive_risk: medium - needs type resolution across modules; foreign types can't be analysed.

rules.title: Don't Debug-log sync records or other user data
rules.problem: `trace!("{:?}", record)` dumps URLs/titles/PII into logs that end up in desktop logs and bug reports.
rules.rule: Types carrying user data (sync records/payloads, logins, tabs) must not be formatted with {:?} in log macros; give them a redacting Display/Debug.
rules.detect: dylint or ast-grep: log-macro args formatted with `:?` whose type is in a sensitive-type list (or defined in */sync/record.rs, *Record/*Payload); alternatively forbid #[derive(Debug)] on those types and require a manual redacting impl.
rules.false_positive_risk: medium - requires maintaining the sensitive-type list; syntactic matching on names is noisy.

rules.title: Build URLs with url::Url APIs, and end base URLs with '/'
rules.problem: Base URLs without a trailing slash lose their last path segment under Url::join; format!-built URLs produce double slashes; relative Location headers fail Url::parse.
rules.rule: Hard-coded base URLs used with join() end in '/', paths are appended with join()/path_segments_mut(), not format!, and redirects are resolved with base.join(location).
rules.detect: ast-grep: const/static/Lazy URL literals with a non-empty path not ending in '/'; `format!("{}/...", $U)` where $U is named *url*/*base*; `Url::parse($LOC)` where $LOC comes from a `location` header.
rules.false_positive_risk: medium - some literals are full endpoints never used as join bases.

rules.title: Check HTTP status before using a response body
rules.problem: Fetching without a status check treats 4xx/5xx error pages as valid content (and caches them).
rules.rule: After send(), call error_for_status()/require_success() or branch on status before reading the body.
rules.detect: ast-grep: in a function, `let $R = $C.send()?` (or chained) followed by `$R.text()`/`.json()`/`.bytes()` with no `error_for_status`, `require_success`, `is_success` or `.status` use in between.
rules.false_positive_risk: medium - status may be checked in a helper the pattern can't see.

rules.title: Avoid blanket #[from] std::io::Error in component errors
rules.problem: A single From<io::Error> variant makes every IO failure look like the same operation (e.g. 'error writing attachment'), hiding the real cause in error reports.
rules.rule: Component error enums use context-specific IO variants built with map_err, not #[from] io::Error; create directories with create_dir_all instead of exists()+create_dir.
rules.detect: ast-grep: `#[from] std::io::Error` / `#[from] io::Error` inside #[derive(thiserror::Error)] enums under components/; pattern `if !$X::exists($D)$$$ { $$$create_dir($D)$$$ }`.
rules.false_positive_risk: high - 9 existing uses (logins, places, nimbus, autofill, ...); only workable as a ratchet on new code.

rules.title: Release foreign callbacks on shutdown and test it
rules.problem: Rust objects that cache Arc<dyn ForeignTrait> keep UniFFI callbacks registered past xpcom-shutdown, triggering desktop leak checks.
rules.rule: Every component holding a foreign callback exposes a shutdown path that drops it, and has a test asserting the callback's strong count reaches 0; engines don't cache their own clones.
rules.detect: Inventory foreign traits (#[uniffi::export(with_foreign)], callback_interface in UDL); for each, require a test that registers an Arc stub, calls shutdown/close, and asserts Weak::strong_count()==0; a custom lint listing struct fields of type Arc<dyn ForeignTrait>.
rules.false_positive_risk: medium - inventory is easy, but proving that every holder is reachable from shutdown needs manual review.

rules.title: No wildcard arms in state-machine transition matches
rules.problem: A catch-all `_ => invalid_transition` arm hides (state, event) pairs nobody considered, e.g. Disconnect or BeginOAuthFlow while Authenticating.
rules.rule: Enable clippy::wildcard_enum_match_arm in state-machine modules so every event is handled explicitly per state.
rules.detect: #![warn(clippy::wildcard_enum_match_arm)] at the top of fxa-client state_machine modules (and other FSMs).
rules.false_positive_risk: low within the scoped modules, but it only forces a decision; it can't pick the right transition.

rules.title: Detect re-acquiring a held DB mutex
rules.problem: Calling a constructor that locks the DB while a lock_db() guard is alive deadlocks the non-reentrant mutex.
rules.rule: Don't call functions that acquire lock_db() while holding a lock_db() guard; smoke-test every public store method.
rules.detect: Intra-crate call-graph script (rust-analyzer/syn): mark fns whose bodies call `.lock_db()`/`db.lock()`; flag calls to marked fns in a scope where a guard from the same lock is live. Runtime alternative: parking_lot deadlock_detection or try_lock_for(timeout) in test builds.
rules.false_positive_risk: medium - guard liveness and indirect calls are approximated.

rules.title: Initialize NSS automatically in tests
rules.problem: Tests that touch crypto without nss::ensure_initialized() fail intermittently depending on test order and threads.
rules.rule: Crates depending on nss/rc_crypto initialize NSS through a shared test helper/ctor so individual tests can't forget it.
rules.detect: cfg(test) #[ctor] (or a test-wrapper macro) in each crate depending on nss; CI script listing such crates whose tests call crypto APIs with no initializer.
rules.false_positive_risk: medium - static detection of 'calls crypto' is approximate; the ctor approach has none.

rules.title: Keep GitHub Actions current and use a shared Rust setup
rules.problem: Deprecated action versions (upload/download-artifact@v3) and ad-hoc rustup installs (wrong PATH, missing toolchain install) broke workflows repeatedly.
rules.rule: Dependabot updates github-actions; workflows use one shared Rust setup step; actionlint runs on workflow changes.
rules.detect: dependabot.yml github-actions ecosystem; grep failing on `uses: actions/(upload|download)-artifact@v[1-3]` and on inline `sh.rustup.rs` in .github/workflows; actionlint.
rules.false_positive_risk: low.

rules.title: Treat new @Deprecated on public Kotlin/Swift API as breaking
rules.problem: Consumers like Fenix compile with -Werror, so adding @Deprecated breaks their build just like an API removal.
rules.rule: Adding @Deprecated / @available(*, deprecated) to public binding APIs requires the breaking-change process (consumer patches ready).
rules.detect: Diff check on PRs: added lines matching `@Deprecated(` under components/*/android/src/main or `@available(*, deprecated` in Swift sources fail unless the PR has a breaking-change label / CHANGELOG breaking entry.
rules.false_positive_risk: medium - some deprecations are intentionally coordinated; a label override is needed.

rules.title: Allowlist the generated binding modules that get packaged
rules.problem: Library-mode bindgen generates bindings for every UniFFI crate linked in (e.g. glean_sym), which then ship in the iOS package.
rules.rule: Generated Swift/Kotlin binding files must match a checked-in allowlist per megazord.
rules.detect: After uniffi-bindgen-library-mode, list generated *.swift/*.h/Kotlin packages and diff against megazords/*/bindings-allowlist.txt.
rules.false_positive_risk: low - the allowlist changes only when components are added.

rules.title: Detect unconditional self-recursion in Kotlin wrappers
rules.problem: A Kotlin member named like the imported Rust binding function calls itself instead of the binding, recursing forever.
rules.rule: Flag Kotlin functions whose body unconditionally calls a function with the same name and arity without a receiver.
rules.detect: Custom detekt rule on KtNamedFunction: sole statement/expression body is a KtCallExpression with the same callee name and argument count and no qualifier; or forbid member functions that share a name with an explicitly imported top-level function.
rules.false_positive_risk: low - legitimate unconditional self-recursion is very rare.
